text:
Mikko Rantanen scored all three Dallas goals, the last one on the power play in overtime, and the Stars beat Boston 3-2 at American Airlines Center to end the Bruins' five-game winning streak. His backhand at 3:52 of overtime finished a night in which Dallas outplayed Boston for long stretches and had to wait for the result to match.

The game opened the other way. Matthew Poitras gave Boston the lead 2:09 into the first period with a snap shot, and James Hagens tipped one in during the second to put the Bruins up 2-1 after Rantanen had tied it once. Rantanen tied it again late in the third. By expected goals, which measure the quality of chances rather than the goals themselves, Dallas finished at 4.06 to Boston's 2.20, and the Stars attempted 66 shots to 43. Using those chances to simulate the game over and over, Dallas wins about 79 percent of the time. Jeremy Swayman kept Boston in it, stopping 22 of 25 shots, about a goal more than the chances he faced would normally allow. Wyatt Johnston had a 39 percent look in overtime that missed the net before Rantanen got his.

Boston also went 0 for 4 on the power play, while Dallas converted its only goal-scoring chance with the man advantage at the right moment. For the Bruins, the run of five straight wins is over. Dallas has now won three in a row.
